reflections.title: Partners in the Family of God

reflect.text: As Paul finishes his letter, he passes along warm greetings from the friends standing with him. These companions came from different backgrounds and served in varied ways. Tertius wrote down Paul's words, Gaius welcomed the church into his home, Erastus worked as the city treasurer, and other helpers were Paul's own countrymen. Even an apostle needed faithful partners to carry out his work. God created us for mutual support, and no Christian is meant to live or serve alone.

Among these workers stands Quartus, who is simply introduced as our brother. He had no public title or fame, yet he wanted to send his love across the sea to believers he had probably never met. As F. B. Meyer observes, his quiet presence reminds us to be content living unknown, as long as our lives are marked by genuine love. The good news of Jesus breaks down barriers and unites people of every background into one single family under God.

questions: Who has God placed in your life to encourage and serve alongside you?
How can you show quiet love to other believers in God's family, including those you may never meet in person?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank you for welcoming us into your family and giving us brothers and sisters to walk with. Help us to value the partners you place around us and never try to follow you on our own. Give us humble hearts that seek no earthly praise, but are simply known for loving your people. Amen.
